Conversation, family & daily routines

careful, don’t fall phrase

also careful, stand still

classical

Plaut. Most. 324

Cavē nē cadās; astā.

careful you don’t fall; stand still

In Libellus VII the boy sings it to himself as he climbs.

Examples

  • Pater «Cavē nē cadās,» inquit; quod puer, dum scandit, ipse sibi cantat.

    Dad said “Careful you don’t fall”; and the boy sings it to himself as he climbs.Libellus VII, Diēs ūnus Osoitsae

  • Cavē nē cadās, astā.

    Careful you don’t fall; stand still (Plaut. Most. 324, in the Libellus II gloss).Libellus II, Sintra: castellum et puteus

  • Ad pinnās, nōn ad marginem.

    Stay by the wall, not by the edge.composed

  • Hoc facitō; hoc fugitō.

    Do this; avoid that.Ter. Ad. 417

See also fall, don’t touch, mind your fingers.

SourcesLewis & Short: caveo · Lewis & Short: asto

Theodōrus et pater · Ad Larem avītum, Libellī I–VII, as they stood on 7 November 2026, with their glosses. Examples marked “Libellus” quote those texts word for word; classical passages are cited by author.
